title: Maximize Points After Choosing K Tasks
summary: Given two arrays of task points and a minimum requirement for technique 1 tasks, determine the maximum total points by completing at least the required number of tasks with technique 1 and the rest with either technique.
statement: Given two arrays of task points and a minimum requirement for technique 1 tasks, determine the maximum total points by completing at least the required number of tasks with technique 1 and the rest with either technique.
constraints: Both technique arrays contain the same up to 100,000 positive scores.
Choose exactly one technique per task, using technique one for at least k tasks.
hints: Start with technique two everywhere; switching task i changes the total by technique1[i]-technique2[i].
Sort these gains descending, take the first k even if negative, then take every remaining nonnegative gain.
Add all selected gains to the technique-two baseline.
Any feasible choice omitting a larger forced gain for a smaller one improves by exchange, and optional positive gains always help.
editorial: Any feasible choice omitting a larger forced gain for a smaller one improves by exchange, and optional positive gains always help.

tests.explanation: Use technique one on scores two and ten and technique two on ten, totaling twenty-two.
Technique one is better on every task, so choosing it throughout gives sixty.
